title.canonicalEnglish: Run and manage CPN-based workflow factories

description.canonicalEnglish:
Run and manage CPN-based workflow factories.

What:
CPN-based workflow factory CLI for running factories, submitting work, and inspecting live sessions.

How to use:
Run you run --work ./docs/examples/startup-work.json to start the current Factory with explicit Work and the local dashboard (http://localhost:7437/dashboard/ui).
Use you run --dir factory --work ./docs/examples/startup-work.json for an explicit Factory directory. See you <cmd> --help for subcommand details.

Agents:
Start with you docs agents for orientation, you submit or you submit batch to enqueue work, and you session list to confirm a live factory.
Run you docs for all packaged reference topics. Use --verbose or --debug for stderr diagnostics; full policy in you docs.

usage.example:
# Start the default Codex-backed Factory with explicit Work.
  you run --work ./docs/examples/startup-work.json

  # Agent orientation and command matrix.
  you docs agents

title.canonicalEnglish: List, open, and close factory sessions on a running host

description.canonicalEnglish:
Manage factory sessions on a running you-agent-factory service.

Subcommands:
  list       list live workspace sessions or durable Factory Sessions with --scope live|persisted|all
  show       show one live or durable Factory Session from GET /factory-sessions/{session_id}
  dispatches list durable Factory Session dispatches from GET /factory-sessions/{session_id}/dispatches
  pause      pause one live or durable Factory Session through POST /factory-sessions/{session_id}/pause
  resume     resume one paused live or durable Factory Session through POST /factory-sessions/{session_id}/resume
  create     open another live session from a folder path
  delete     close a live session by session id

Durable list output uses Factory Session status, source identity, result availability, progress, and action availability. Session commands use the same default --port as work list. Use --json to emit API-shaped responses on stdout; diagnostics stay on stderr when --verbose or --debug is set.

usage.example:
# List live sessions on the default local port.
  you session list

  # Show orchestrator-aware runtime for one live session.
  you session show session-beta

  # Pause and resume the default compatibility session.
  you session pause
  you session resume

  # Pause and resume one named or durable Factory Session.
  you session pause session-beta
  you session resume dur-sess-js-run-n-001

  # Emit API-shaped JSON for automation.
  you session list --json

  # Open and close sessions on a non-default port.
  you session create --dir /workspace/fleet --port 9090
  you session delete session-beta --port 9090 --json

  # Pause and resume the default compatibility session.
  you session pause
  you session resume

  # Target a different service port for list output.
  you session list --port 9090

description.canonicalEnglish:
Show one live factory session from GET /factory-sessions/{session_id}.

Human output uses FactorySession as the canonical runtime noun and prints orchestrator kind plus Petri or JavaScript runtime projections. Dynamic workflow wording appears only as JavaScript shorthand. Omit session-id to target the default compatibility session (~default). Use global --json for the API-shaped FactorySession payload and global --server to target the same factory API base URI as work list and factory query.

usage.example:
# Show the default compatibility factory session.
  you session show

  # Show one named live session with orchestrator-aware runtime fields.
  you session show session-beta

  # Emit API-shaped JSON for automation.
  you --json session show session-beta

description.canonicalEnglish:
Print packaged markdown reference topics from the installed binary.

Run without a topic to print the quick-start blurb and packaged docs index. Use one supported topic argument to print the authored markdown page with no wrapper formatting.

usage.example:
# Print the packaged docs index and quick-start blurb.
  you docs

  # Print one authored reference topic.
  you docs agents

title.canonicalEnglish: Inspect discovered models from a running service

description.canonicalEnglish:
Inspect discovered models from a running infinite-you service.

Use list to discover model identifiers, inspect to view one model's readiness and capabilities, invoke to call a discovered model directly through the shared in-process bootstrap, and pull to populate the managed local-model cache for supported local assets.

usage.example:
# List models exposed by the default local service.
  you models list

  # Inspect one model readiness surface.
  you models inspect OMNIVOICE_Q4_K_M

  # Pull managed local assets before invoking.
  you models pull OMNIVOICE_Q4_K_M

description.canonicalEnglish: List discovered models from GET /models on the configured service. Human output summarizes provider locality, supported operations, managed-runtime readiness, and resource counts. Use global --json for API-shaped output and global --server to target a non-default factory API base URI.

usage.example:
# List models on the default local service.
  you models list

  # Emit API-shaped JSON for automation.
  you --json models list

description.canonicalEnglish: Inspect one discovered model from GET /models/{model_name}. Human output prints readiness, lifecycle, capabilities, and diagnostics for the named model. Use global --json for API-shaped output and global --server to target a non-default factory API base URI.

usage.example:
# Inspect one model on the default local service.
  you models inspect OMNIVOICE_Q4_K_M

  # Emit API-shaped JSON for automation.
  you --json models inspect OMNIVOICE_Q4_K_M

description.canonicalEnglish: Invoke one discovered model through the shared in-process bootstrap. Requires a model name, an uppercase --operation, non-empty --text, and either --output for streamed audio or global --json for structured invocation metadata. Readiness-gated execution uses the current factory configuration without starting a full workflow.

examples: you models invoke OMNIVOICE_Q4_K_M --operation TTS --text "Read the release summary." --output ./speech.wav
you --json models invoke OMNIVOICE_Q4_K_M --operation TTS --text "Read the release summary."

usage.example:
# Stream TTS audio to a file.
  you models invoke OMNIVOICE_Q4_K_M --operation TTS --text "Read the release summary." --output ./speech.wav

  # Emit structured invocation metadata.
  you --json models invoke OMNIVOICE_Q4_K_M --operation TTS --text "Read the release summary."

title.canonicalEnglish: Pull one discovered local model into the managed cache

description.canonicalEnglish: Pull one discovered local model into the managed cache through POST /models/{model_name}/pull. Human output reports pull outcome, readiness, cache path, revision, and downloaded files. Use global --json for API-shaped output and global --server to target a non-default factory API base URI.

usage.example:
# Pull managed local assets for one model.
  you models pull OMNIVOICE_Q4_K_M

  # Emit API-shaped JSON for automation.
  you --json models pull OMNIVOICE_Q4_K_M
